# C5 — ISA dispatch corpus

Synthetic ELF64 / PE32+ stubs used by `EXP-MACHINE-DISPATCH` to verify that
`Filters50::detect_filter` dispatches on the container machine field instead of
defaulting every executable to the x86 `E8` transform.

## Provenance

Generated by `tools/generate_c5_corpus.py` (seed `1337`, fixed payload length):

```
python tools/generate_c5_corpus.py --out tests/fixtures/c5
```

| File | Container | `e_machine` / `Machine` | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|
| `elf_x86_64.o` | ELF64 `ET_REL` | `0x3E` | `E8 rel32` calls, NOPs, filler |
| `elf_aarch64.o` | ELF64 `ET_REL` | `0xB7` | `BL imm26` and `NOP` words |
| `elf_riscv64.o` | ELF64 `ET_REL` | `0xF3` | `JAL` and `NOP` words |
| `pe_x86_64.exe` | PE32+ | `0x8664` | `E8 rel32` calls, NOPs, filler |
| `pe_aarch64.exe` | PE32+ | `0xAA64` | `BL imm26` and `NOP` words |

`manifest.sha256` pins every fixture and is written LF-only, so
`sha256sum -c manifest.sha256` works from any host. The repository-wide
`*.o` ignore rule is overridden by this directory's `.gitignore`.

## Size gate

The gate is "no C5 member grows relative to a binary built from `main`". It is
measured with `tools/measure_c5.py`, which builds one non-solid, single-member
archive per fixture and compression level and re-extracts it to confirm the
original bytes:

```
python tools/measure_c5.py \
    --baseline main=/path/to/main/build/openrar64/Release/openrar.exe \
    --candidate branch=build/openrar64/Release/openrar.exe
```

Measured 2026-11-12 against `main` (`c5ff210`) and `exp/machine-dispatch`
(`e187970`), archive bytes:

| Member | `-m0` main → branch (Δ) | `-m1` | `-m3` | `-m5` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `elf_x86_64.o` | 10,227 → 10,227 (0) | 8,961 → 8,961 (0) | 8,961 → 8,961 (0) | 8,961 → 8,961 (0) |
| `elf_aarch64.o` | 10,229 → 10,229 (0) | 5,570 → 5,570 (0) | 5,538 → 5,538 (0) | 5,521 → 5,521 (0) |
| `elf_riscv64.o` | 10,229 → 10,229 (0) | 5,076 → 5,076 (0) | 4,957 → 4,957 (0) | 4,909 → 4,909 (0) |
| `pe_x86_64.exe` | 10,677 → 10,677 (0) | 9,059 → 9,059 (0) | 9,054 → 9,054 (0) | 9,051 → 9,051 (0) |
| `pe_aarch64.exe` | 10,679 → 10,679 (0) | 5,737 → 5,731 (**−6**) | 5,696 → 5,690 (**−6**) | 5,688 → 5,682 (**−6**) |

**Result: PASS.** Four members are byte-identical to `main`, because dispatch
returns the same filter they already received (x86 controls keep `E8`;
`elf_aarch64`/`elf_riscv64` were already `None` by accident of the density
scan). `pe_aarch64` is the only member whose decision changes — `main` applies
`E8` to every unrecognised PE machine, the branch returns `None` — and it is
6 bytes smaller for it at `-m1/-m3/-m5`.

### Corpus revision note

The first revision of this corpus reused the stubs from `build/c2_c5_eval/`,
whose `pe_arm64.exe` payload was **x86-shaped** (101 `0xE8` bytes in an ARM64
container). On that fixture suppressing `E8` cost 6 bytes at `-m3`/`-m5`
(557 vs 551) and 2 bytes at `-m1`; that measurement is real but says nothing
about ARM64 code, which rarely produces a dense run of valid `E8 rel32`
candidates. It is recorded here for the audit trail and is **not** a gate
result. The committed fixtures carry ISA-shaped payloads; the old stub is not
part of the corpus.

## Non-gating control

`control_pe_aarch64_x86payload.exe` is the **original** stub from the first
C2/C5 eval, carried over byte-for-byte (SHA-256
`37cc3d2bb0089190878a29911d72319194c03ce9c6b26c5612c2968fb85acce8`); the
generator does not rewrite it. It is a 70-byte PE header with machine `0xAA64`
followed by 10,000 bytes of x86-shaped payload containing 101 `0xE8` bytes —
x86 code in an ARM64 container.

It exists so the corpus swap cannot be read as moving the goalposts. Measured
by `tools/measure_c5.py`:

| level | main | branch | Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `-m1` | 604 | 606 | **+2 B** |
| `-m3` | 587 | 593 | **+6 B** |
| `-m5` | 585 | 591 | **+6 B** |

That is the real cost of suppressing a filter that happened to fit x86-shaped
bytes. It is **excluded from the gate**: the gate is about ARM64 code, and this
file is not ARM64 code. The +6 B is recorded here as an explicit, documented
exception rather than averaged away or dropped.

**Those absolute sizes are not comparable with the earlier `551`/`557` unless the
stored name is accounted for.** RAR5 stores the member name in UTF-16 (2 bytes
per character), and this control's descriptive 33-character name is 18
characters longer than the original `c5_pe_arm64.exe`. Archived under that
original name the same bytes measure **568 / 551 / 549 B** for `main` and
**570 / 557 / 555 B** for the branch at `-m1/-m3/-m5` — exactly the
`551 → 557` the first analysis reported. Only the deltas are name-independent;
`587`/`593` minus the 36-byte name cost is `551`/`557`, not a contradiction.

## Real corpus (CI)

These are **not compiler output**. The Windows reference host has no clang
(Q-7), so the real objects are produced in the Ubuntu CI leg from
[`pinned.c`](pinned.c) — freestanding, no headers, no sysroot, SHA-256
`6305cf3e5e80b24b9d4795f1de6e7783229332dffd8fd57ed55f691006744828`:

```
python3 tools/build_c5_real_corpus.py --out build/c5_real
```

which runs, per target:

```
clang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu -O2 -c pinned.c -o elf_aarch64.o
clang --target=riscv64-linux-gnu -O2 -c pinned.c -o elf_riscv64.o
clang --target=x86_64-linux-gnu  -O2 -c pinned.c -o elf_x86_64.o
```

The builder verifies the source hash and each object's `e_machine`, and it
refuses to emit an x86-64 control that does not reach the detector's 32-valid-
`E8` threshold — otherwise the size gate would not exercise the filter at all.

`.github/workflows/wave1-c5-parity.yml` builds `main` and the branch with
clang, generates that corpus, and re-runs both checks on the real objects:
`tools/measure_c5.py` (size gate, `--allow-missing` because only the three ELF
objects exist) and `tools/prove_dispatch_parity.py` (30 ratchet cells plus
reference extraction of changed archives). Reference extraction is UnRAR-only
on Linux: WinRAR has no Linux CLI, so the WinRAR half stays on the Windows leg.

Size deltas on the committed stubs are evidence about **dispatch and filter
overhead**, not about compression ratio on real ARM64/RISC-V code. The CI
numbers are the ones that speak to real compiler output.
